key_insight: Static train-test splits overstate forecasting performance for foundation-style time-series models because they enable contamination and don't reflect changing realities; a live, continuously-updated benchmark reveals true temporal generalization. Impermanent provides a leak-resistant, rolling evaluation that measures how models perform on genuinely future data.
problem_solved: Addresses evaluation contamination and unrealistic stationarity assumptions in time-series forecasting benchmarks by preventing training or model-selection on test data and by measuring model performance under temporal distribution shift.
method: Live rolling-evaluation protocol: continuously release new future test windows and score models on genuinely unseen time slices instead of fixed splits.
Strict data/version controls and automated evaluation pipeline: block test data access, log submissions, and compute temporal robustness metrics to avoid leakage or post-hoc tuning on test scores.
Public leaderboard and monitoring: track model performance over time, highlight degradation under distribution shifts, and enable reproducible comparisons for foundation-style forecasting models.
impact: Provides practitioners and researchers a more trustworthy, deployment-relevant measurement of forecasting models' temporal robustness, helping select models that actually generalize to future data and avoid overstated claims from contaminated evaluations.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing rolling train/test windows moving forward in time (live evaluation vs static split)

paper_title: Impermanent: A Live Benchmark for Temporal Generalization in Time Series Forecasting
paper_authors: Azul Garza, Renée Rosillo, Rodrigo Mendoza-Smith, David Salinas, Andrew Robert Williams
